title: Patch: a queued player is told when the server can't be reached, instead of reading that they are in the queue through the outage
thread:
**Issue #3792 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #3792: Patch: a queued player is told when the server can't be reached, instead of reading that they are in the queue through the outage Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot. ## What it actually means While you wait in the queue for an online game, your page checks in with the server every couple of seconds. The server drops a waiting player it has not heard from in about 12 seconds, so nobody absent gets seated. If your connection drops, those check-ins fail silently. The screen keeps saying "In the queue. You will be taken to the game as soon as someone is found" while the server has already taken you out, and you only find out once the connection comes back. Once this is built, after a few failed check-ins the queue screen says "Can't reach the server. Still trying…", and the notice goes away at the first check-in that succeeds. ## Why - `apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx:422-447`: the wait's account reads end in `.catch(() => undefined)` (`:444`). A failed read changes nothing on screen; only a successful one can end the wait. - The status words stay `queuedStatus` (`play.tsx` around 709). - The server cancels a ticket unheard from for `QUEUE_TICKET_STALE_MS`, 12 s (`crates/server/src/config.rs:600`, R897000). The client reads every `SERIES_POLL_SECONDS`, 2 s, and ends the wait after `QUEUE_ENDED_AFTER_READS`, 2 good reads saying the ticket is gone (`apps/web/src/wire/serverConfig.ts:127,139`). So an outage of more than 12 s cancels the ticket, while the screen claims otherwise until the network returns. - Other screens already say when the connection is gone: the match bar's "Reconnecting…" (`apps/web/src/game/connectionWords.ts:13`) and the deck workshop's offline state (`apps/web/src/game/deckbuilder/sync.ts:372`). ## Proposal - `useLobbyWatch` counts failed reads in a row. Past a named constant in the web's own config (rule 9), for example 3 (about 6 s, inside the server's 12 s), the queue and room waits show one `role="status"` notice, "Can't reach the server. Still trying…", beside their status line. - The first good read clears the notice and resets the count. - The ticket logic stays as it is: R897000's ended-reads count and the pairing navigation do not change. - A zh-CN entry for the words. - A ruling in this issue's block (the client says when it cannot reach the server, as the match bar does), with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/.md` and a test named after it. ## Where it lands `apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx` and `play.test.tsx`, the web's config and zh-CN strings, `spec/rulings/R.md`, `spec/pending/.md`. SPEC §9.5 (the queue), R897000, R3205000. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] With fake timers: account reads rejecting with `ApiUnreachableError` for the constant's count show the notice, and the queue line stays. - [ ] Fewer failures than that show nothing. - [ ] A good read after the notice clears it. - [ ] When reads come back saying the ticket is gone, the existing queue-ended path still runs, and the R897000 tests in `play.test.tsx` stay green. - [ ] The threshold is a named constant, and the client restates no server number. - [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/play.test.tsx` and `cargo jackioh spec check` are green. ## Size and risks Small to medium: one hook, one line on screen, tests and a ruling. `difficulty:medium`. Risk: a flaky but working connection flashes the notice. The threshold keeps one or two failed reads silent. --- Suggested by @jgoetzmann-bot while the queue was empty. Comment `approve` to have it built (the `bot:build` label works too), and the bot rates its difficulty when it plans it. Comment `reject` to close it without building it. Class: `polish` → `priority:medium`; relabel to change it. ## Plan _Written by `claude-8` (claude, `sonnet`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43310799356)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal A player waiting in the online queue or a room wait is told "Can't reach the server. Still trying…" after `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` (3) account reads in a row fail because the server cannot be reached. The queue line stays beside the notice. The first good read clears the notice and resets the count. The ticket logic does not change: R897000's `QUEUE_ENDED_AFTER_READS` count, the pairing navigation and `queuedStatus` stay as they are. The threshold is a named client-side constant, and the client restates no server number. The work adds a zh-CN string, a ruling R3792000 with its §11 paragraph in `spec/pending/3792.md`, and tests. ## Files to touch | File | Kind | What changes | |---|---|---| | `apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx` | change | Add `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS`. Add `unreachable: "play-unreachable"` to `playTestid`. `useLobbyWatch` counts failed reads and returns a boolean. Render the notice in `PlayRoute`. Cite R3792000 in the header comment. | | `apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx` | change | New `describe("R3792000 …")` block with the tests below. | | `apps/web/src/i18n/zh-CN.json` | change | One new entry, placed right after the `"Your queue expired. Find a match to queue again."` line (about line 2908). | | `spec/rulings/R3792000.md` | new | The ruling note. | | `spec/pending/3792.md` | new | The §11 paragraph. | Do not touch `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `.claude/`, any crate, `apps/web/src/wire/`, `spec/11-rulings.md` or `spec/INDEX.md`. Never run `cargo jackioh spec index`. Governing spec: §9.5 (the queue), R897000, R3205000, R3207003, CLAUDE.md rules 7 and 9. Decisions the issue did not settle: - **Constant location:** it lives in `play.tsx`, as `landing.tsx` does with `QUESTS_UNROLL_MS`. A new `routes/config.ts` was rejected as a new module for one number. - **What counts as a failure:** only `ApiUnreachableError`, which `api.ts` throws for a transport failure or timeout. An `ApiRequestError` such as a 5xx means the server answered, so it counts as reached and resets the count instead of showing "can't reach". Counting every rejection was rejected because it would call a 401 an outage. - **No import of `QUEUE_TICKET_STALE_MS`:** it is not in `serverConfig.ts`, and the client must not copy it. 3 × `SERIES_POLL_SECONDS` is 6 s, inside the server's 12 s, and the ruling states that in words. - **Notice placement:** a separate `

` after the status line, not new text inside it. Putting the notice into `statusWords` was rejected because `Status` is a single kind and the queue line must stay. ## Steps 1. **`play.tsx`, constants and testid.** Under `MS_PER_SECOND` / `SECONDS_PER_MINUTE` (about lines 73–74) add: ```ts /** R3792000: account reads of a wait failing in a row (the server unreachable) before the screen says so; at SERIES_POLL_SECONDS apart it is inside the server's ticket timeout (R897000). */ export const LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS = 3; ``` Add `unreachable: "play-unreachable",` to `playTestid`, after `status`. 2. **`play.tsx`, imports.** Add `ApiUnreachableError` to the value imports from `"../net/api.ts"`. Its mocked-module spread in the test keeps the real class. 3. **`play.tsx`, `useLobbyWatch`.** Change the return type from `void` to `boolean` (true means "unreachable"). Update its doc comment: R3792000 says the hook returns whether the wait's reads have failed unreachable `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` times in a row. - Add `const failedReads = useRef(0);` next to `endedReads`. - Add `const [unreachable, setUnreachable] = useState(false);`. - In the effect's `if (!waiting)` block (which resets `ended` and `endedReads`), also set `failedReads.current = 0; setUnreachable(false);`. - In `check`'s `.then((me) => …)`, replace the first line `if (canceled || navigated.current || ended.current) return;` with: ```ts if (canceled) return; // R3792000: an answer of any kind proves the server was reached. failedReads.current = 0; setUnreachable(false); if (navigated.current || ended.current) return; ``` - Replace `.catch(() => undefined)` with: ```ts .catch((cause: unknown) => { if (canceled || !waiting) return; if (cause instanceof ApiUnreachableError) { failedReads.current += 1; if (failedReads.current >= LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS) setUnreachable(true); } else { // The server answered (a refusal, a 5xx): reached, so the count starts again. failedReads.current = 0; setUnreachable(false); } }) ``` - End the hook with `return waiting && unreachable;`. - Do not change the R897000 `endedReads` logic, `navigated`/`ended`, or the interval and `pageWake` wiring. 4. **`play.tsx`, `PlayRoute`.** - Change `useLobbyWatch(token, waiting, goFound, onQueueEnded, queueWait, me);` (about line 840) to `const unreachable = useLobbyWatch(…same args…);`. - In the JSX, directly after the `{status !== null ? (…) : null}` block (about line 1053) add: ```tsx {unreachable ? (

{t("Can't reach the server. Still trying…")}

) : null} ``` - `lobby.css` already styles `.tavern.play-screen > .notice`, so no CSS change is needed. - Add `R3792000` to the header comment's R-list at the top of the file (line 1–2). 5. **`zh-CN.json`.** After the `"Your queue expired. …"` entry add `"Can't reach the server. Still trying…": "无法连接服务器。仍在重试…",`. Keep the straight apostrophe and the `…` character, as `"Couldn't reach JackiOh. …"` does. 6. **`spec/rulings/R3792000.md`.** Use this front matter, then the body: ``` --- id: R3792000 title: "A queued or room-waiting player is told when the server cannot be reached (issue #3792; amends R897000)" cards: "§9.5, R897000, R3205000, R3207003, issue #3792" proven_in: - apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx --- ``` Body, with `[[R897000]]` and `[[§9.5]]` written as links: - **Problem:** the wait's account reads end in a silent catch, so a dropped connection left "In the queue" on screen after the server had cancelled the unheard ticket ([[R897000]], 12 s). - **Rule:** `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` (3, about 6 s) transport failures in a row (`ApiUnreachableError`) make the queue and room waits show one `role="status"` notice, "Can't reach the server. Still trying…", beside the status line. The queue line stays. - **Clearing:** any read the server answered clears the notice and resets the count. A non-transport rejection also resets it. - **Ticket logic:** unchanged. R897000's ended-reads count and the pairing navigation work as before, and a failed read counts as neither a gone-ticket nor a good read. - **Idle:** a lobby that is not waiting shows nothing. - **Rule 7:** presentation only; the server still owns the ticket. - **Hearthstone semantics:** the "Reconnecting…" banner. - **Rejected:** counting every rejected read; a notice inside the status text. 7. **`spec/pending/3792.md`.** One paragraph in the folded style, in the shape `**[[R3792000]] (issue #3792, 2026-11-12)**: amends [[R897000]]. …`. It is a summary of step 6 in 3–4 sentences, with no `---` front matter. ## Tests All in `apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx`. Add `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` to the imports from `"./play.tsx"` and `ApiUnreachableError` to the imports from `"../net/api.ts"`. Put the new tests in a new `describe("R3792000 the wait says when the server cannot be reached", …)` next to the R3207000 describe at the end of the file. Copy that block's pattern: - `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["setInterval", "clearInterval"] })` and `afterEach(() => { vi.useRealTimers(); })`. - `rememberQueued("bo1")`, `render(<PlayRoute token={TOKEN} />)`, then `await settle({ advance: 0 })` and `await settle({ advance: SERIES_POLL_SECONDS * 1000 })` to move one read at a time (`settle` is from `../test/settle.ts`). - Helper `const down = (): void => { vi.mocked(getMe).mockRejectedValue(new ApiUnreachableError(new TypeError("Failed to fetch"))); };`. Tests, each named with `R3792000` as a word, since `spec check` matches on it: 1. `it("R3792000 the constant's count of unreachable reads shows the notice and keeps the queue line")`: `down()`, mount (read 1). Advance the poll period `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS - 1` more times. Assert `playTestid.unreachable` is present with text "Can't reach the server. Still trying…", `role="status"`, and that `playTestid.status` still contains `queuedStatus`-style text. (The queued status only exists after enqueue, so set it up with `renderLobby()`, `enqueue` mocked `openTicket("bo1")`, and a click on `playTestid.queue`. Mount with `getMe` resolving `me(null)` first, then call `down()` before advancing.) Also assert `playTestid.searching` is present. 2. `it("R3792000 fewer failed reads than the constant show nothing")`: the same setup, but stop one read short. `queryByTestId(playTestid.unreachable)` is null. This is the criterion that the flaky-link threshold stays silent. 3. `it("R3792000 a good read after the notice clears it and starts the count again")`: reach the notice, then `vi.mocked(getMe).mockResolvedValue({ ...me(null), queued: true })`, advance one period, and assert the notice is gone. Then `down()` and advance `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS - 1` periods and assert no notice (the count restarted). 4. `it("R3792000 reads saying the ticket is gone still end the wait after the notice")`: reach the notice, then `mockResolvedValue({ ...me(null), queued: false })`. After `QUEUE_ENDED_AFTER_READS` periods assert the text "Your queue expired. Find a match to queue again.", the notice gone, and `readQueued()` null. 5. `it("R3792000 a read the server refused is not an unreachable one")`: `getMe` rejects `new ApiRequestError(...)`. Check the real constructor signature in `net/api.ts` (grep `class ApiRequestError`) and follow how other tests in this file build one. Advance more than the constant's count and assert there is no notice. 6. `it("R3792000 a room wait shows the notice too")`: `createRoom` resolves `{ code: "QRST", expiresAt: 0, mode: "random" }`, as in the R897000 room test. Then `down()` and advance past the count. Assert the notice and `playTestid.roomCode`. 7. `it("R3792000 an idle lobby never shows it")`: no queue, `down()`, mount and advance well past the count. No notice. 8. `it("R3792000 the count's wait is inside the server's ticket timeout")`: assert `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS` is at least 2 (one failed read stays silent) and `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS * SERIES_POLL_SECONDS` is less than 12. Do not export or import a server timeout here, and do not add a 12 literal: use `QUEUE_ENDED_AFTER_READS * SERIES_POLL_SECONDS * 6` as the stated bound only if you need one. Otherwise drop this test, since the ruling text states the relation. Existing tests must stay green. Notably, "ignores a failed read rather than surfacing it as a lobby error" (a plain `Error`, not waiting) and the three R897000 tests need no edit. Commands: ``` pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/play.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck pnpm exec eslint apps/web/src/routes/play.tsx apps/web/src/routes/play.test.tsx pnpm --dir apps/web test src/i18n cargo jackioh spec check ``` ## Done when - [ ] After 3 unreachable reads in a row the queue wait shows the `role="status"` notice and the queue line stays (test 1). - [ ] 2 failed reads show nothing (test 2). - [ ] A good read clears the notice and resets the count (test 3). - [ ] The queue-ended path and the R897000 tests are unchanged and green (test 4). - [ ] The room wait shows the notice too (test 6). - [ ] The threshold is the named `LOBBY_UNREACHABLE_AFTER_READS`, and no server number is restated. - [ ] zh-CN entry added, and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/i18n` is green. - [ ] `spec/rulings/R3792000.md` and `spec/pending/3792.md` exist, `spec/11-rulings.md` and `spec/INDEX.md` are untouched, and `cargo jackioh spec check` is green. - [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/routes/play.test.tsx`, web typecheck, eslint and `cargo fmt --check` pass. - [ ] No `eslint-disable`, `@ts-ignore`, skipped test or lowered check. ## Risks - A `setState` in the catch after unmount or an effect re-run is guarded by `canceled`. The success path resets before the `navigated`/`ended` early-return, so a late good read clears the notice but never re-navigates. - The `waiting` closure in the catch is the effect run's own value. The effect re-runs when `waiting` changes, so a stale run is `canceled`. - `reading` and `pageWake` are untouched. The notice never blocks the leave or cancel buttons. - The notice only affects rendering. No engine, wire or server change, so `apps/web/src/wire` stays clean. - `spec check` fails if `R3792000` is cited in code without the note, or if the test titles lack the word. The header comment cites it, so the note must exist. ## Open questions None. The one judgment call is that only `ApiUnreachableError` counts as a failed read; a person can widen it later. <!-- /jackioh-bot:plan --> --- Comment by @MaxGoetzmann at 2026-11-12T21:23:20Z: Approve ````
